'''SBD''' was a common unit of measurement for [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]]. The value indicated how much damage the vessel could withstand before the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] started taking damage.

From [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], vessels equipped with a deflector measured the shield recharge rate with SBD. It was often followed by the vessel's hull rating, measured in [[RU/Legends|RU]]. For example, a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]] starfighter shields were rated at 50 SBD with a 20 RU rated hull. By comparison, an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] shields were measured at 4800 SBD with a 2272 RU rated hull. The Executor-class star dreadnought had a shield power of 96,000 SBD.

The SBD rating for some vessels appeared to vary based on whether the information came from an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] or [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] source.

==Behind the scenes==
SBD was first used in the 1993 LucasArts starfighter simulator, [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]. It was later defined in ''[[The Stele Chronicles]]'', a short booklet included in the package of the LucasArts PC [[Star Wars video games|video game]], [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']].

The term was consistently used in subsequent games including ''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'', ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter]], ''and ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''. Different systems of shield measurement are used by the [[West End Games]] and [[Wizards of the Coast]] role-playing games and by the [[Dark Forces/Jedi Knight|''Dark Forces'']] series of video games.
